builder_plan.scenario: Your workload might fit a smaller or differently structured model.
builder_plan.change: Check for available weights and a compatible runtime before planning a product trial.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current model on identical held-out tasks and the same resource budget.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Task success, latency, memory, context limits, and migration cost.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Dory1.0-4B: A Looped Normalized-GPT
summary: Replaces fixed-depth inference and the need to deploy larger checkpoints with a single 4B checkpoint whose shared recurrent block is applied a variable number of times, trading extra latent compute for accuracy instead of longer outputs or bigger models. Costs additional latency and compute per generated token roughly proportional to loop count, requires inference-stack support for looped execution (non-standard serving code), and the reported gains stem from a 6-trillion-token pre-training run plus NVFP4 training and RLVR post-training that the reader cannot replicate. Loop benefits are benchmark- and task-dependent (largest on coding, agentic, long-context), may not transfer to the reader's workload, and tooling for last-loop-only KV caching and difficulty-aware loop routing may be immature outside the authors' release.
rationale: The open weights (BF16, MXFP8, NVFP4, GGUF) fit a 24 GB GPU and the elastic-depth knob directly matches constrained infrastructure, but the gains depend on task mix and non-standard serving support, so it warrants a workload-specific pilot rather than unconditional adoption.
technique: Looped latent-recurrent transformer with elastic depth

claims.statement: Replaces fixed-depth inference and the need to deploy larger checkpoints with a single 4B checkpoint whose shared recurrent block is applied a variable number of times, trading extra latent compute for accuracy instead of longer outputs or bigger models. Costs additional latency and compute per generated token roughly proportional to loop count, requires inference-stack support for looped execution (non-standard serving code), and the reported gains stem from a 6-trillion-token pre-training run plus NVFP4 training and RLVR post-training that the reader cannot replicate. Loop benefits are benchmark- and task-dependent (largest on coding, agentic, long-context), may not transfer to the reader's workload, and tooling for last-loop-only KV caching and difficulty-aware loop routing may be immature outside the authors' release.

With two or more loops the 4B model outperforms Qwen3.5-9B, Gemma 4 12B, and Gemma 4 26B-A4B on average across 12 benchmarks; with four loops it generates 1.3-2.5x fewer tokens on agentic benchmarks, while KV-cache footprint stays equal to a non-looped model.
